analysis.title: Public Policy: What to watch on election night. An hour-by-hour guide of what we will be watching tomorrow night
key_insights: Barclays gives an hour-by-hour guide to the November 3, 2026 US midterm election night, from exit polls at 5pm ET through Alaska at midnight ET.
Exit polls start at 5pm ET and give a first read on whether the electorate's makeup and priorities match pre-election polling.

The first signal on House races comes at 6pm ET from Kentucky's 6th district (R+7) and Indiana's 5th district (R+8). A near-tie or a Democratic lead in either would point to a strong night for Democrats and a possible blue wave.

Georgia and South Carolina close at 7pm ET. Ossoff leads by 8pp in Georgia. Darline Graham is running in a state Trump won by 18pp. A Graham underperformance would signal a broad Democratic wave in deeply Republican (R+15) states. An Ossoff underperformance would signal a weaker Democratic environment than polls show.

Three Florida districts redrawn to favor Republicans (FL-14 and FL-22 at R+4, FL-25 at R+3) are an early test of the Republican redistricting strategy. Democratic holds in FL-14 and FL-25 plus a win in open FL-22 would mean redistricting delivers fewer Republican gains than expected.

Ohio is one of four competitive Senate races in states Trump won by double digits (11.2pp in Ohio), and Barclays says the Democratic path to a Senate majority likely runs through it. Polls close at 7:30pm ET.

North Carolina is a must-win for Democrats to retake the Senate. Roy Cooper leads by nearly 11pp in the RCP average, so the race is an early benchmark of polling accuracy. Results in line with polls would raise confidence in Democratic leads in states that close later.

Texas begins reporting shortly after 8pm ET. Early and mailed ballots come first, which could produce a 'blue mirage' that narrows as Republican-leaning election day votes are counted. A close race may not be called until Wednesday afternoon.

A win by Democratic Texas gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa could send a shock wave through the AI trade, because Texas is the center of the data center buildout and Hinojosa has campaigned on a data center moratorium.
Georgia also has a competitive gubernatorial race worth watching for implications for the state's data center policy.

Maine could decide Senate control. Sen. Collins is the only Republican senator in a Harris-won state and has repeatedly outperformed polls. Maine reports slowly, so control could stay unresolved for days if Maine is pivotal.
Democrats likely need to hold Michigan's Senate seat. Michigan had a 'blue mirage' in 2024, so an early Democratic lead should be read cautiously.
Kansas (last elected a Democratic senator in 1932) and Mississippi (Trump +23 in 2024) test the upper bound of Democratic gains. A competitive Mississippi Senate race would suggest a 'blue tsunami'.
Iowa (Trump +13) is one of six Republican-held competitive Senate seats. Democrats need four of the six for the majority. Polls close at 9pm ET.

New Hampshire and Minnesota are the two Republican pickup opportunities. Barclays calls Minnesota a long shot. A Republican win in Minnesota would force Democrats to win an additional Republican-held seat elsewhere.
Alaska closes at midnight ET and reports slowly. If there is no blue wave, Alaska could decide Senate control, and in that case control may not be known for up to two weeks.
risk_factors: A Democratic win in the Texas governor's race, on a data center moratorium platform, could hit the AI trade.
Slow-reporting states (Maine, Alaska) could leave Senate control unresolved for days to two weeks.
Early 'blue mirage' results in Texas and Michigan could mislead on the final outcome.

tension_points.bull_case: Democratic strength in R+7/R+8 House districts, Graham underperforming in South Carolina, and a competitive Mississippi Senate race would point to a blue wave or 'blue tsunami'.
tension_points.bear_case: Ossoff underperforming his 8pp polling lead would signal a less favorable Democratic environment than polls suggest. Early 'blue mirage' counts in Texas and Michigan could also overstate Democratic strength.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An Ossoff result below his 8pp polling lead in Georgia, or North Carolina results far from Cooper's roughly 11pp polling lead, would undercut the wave case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Senate control may be decided by Maine or Alaska, which report slowly and could leave the result unresolved for days or weeks.
theme_stances.evidence: Maine could therefore be decisive in determining control of the Senate.
